_comment: pl.prywatnyportfel.tax.FxConversion (phone). The phone had none at all until this fixture was
written — it summed holdings and cash across currencies as raw numbers, so a portfolio with
USD and PLN assets reported a net worth the web never showed.
Expected values were generated by calling the Python implementation, not written by hand.
`appliesTo` limits a case to the implementations that can satisfy it. The Kotlin module has no
JSON parser in its main source set, so the string-payload case is web and server only; its
caller converts JSON to a map first.

cases.why: No rate is needed, and none may be invented.
The stored pair is USD/PLN, used as written.
Only USD/PLN is stored, so the reverse direction has to be derived.
No USD/EUR pair exists; the path runs USD to PLN to EUR.
GBP/EUR then EUR/PLN — a hop through a currency that is not the base.
A missing rate must not silently zero a holding; the amount passes through.
Currency codes arrive from imports and forms in mixed case.
An unknown source currency must not be guessed.
Quote providers return USDPLN=X; stored rates may carry that spelling.
The app's own FX tickers carry an FX: prefix.
A zero or negative rate is corrupt data, not a conversion.
Stored state sometimes holds fxRates as a serialised string.
